items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Yeah. Most of them like Tony Jackson and all of them, you know, like that.

ctx.x: Funny fellas, huh? Funny fellas, huh?

Yeah. Says the piano player was funny fellas, huh? Yeah. Yeah. Most of them like Tony Jackson and all of them, you know, like that. And I forget, there was about five or six of them, you know. They said Buddy Christian was one, but they were right enough. They said he wouldn't, you know. He died like one. Yeah, Buddy Christian. He had plenty women, huh? Yeah.
He had plenty women, huh? Yeah.

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: I don't remember Tony Jackson playing with no band, you know. This was a well-known piano player.

ctx.x: Ask him about Tony Jackson. He wanted to tell us about Tony Jackson.

So he wanted to tell us about Tony Jackson. Tony Jackson? Well, Tony Jackson, that fellow was a, you know, this cabinet player. He used to play on hold, you know, all the time. He was a piano player. He used to say he was a morphedizer, you know. And the other part of it too, Bunnell. Both of them was good. But then Bunnell used to high sometimes with piano and banjo. Piano and guitar. Like that, you know. In them little, what do you call them, little beer parties, you know. Just two pieces. I played with them…
I asked him, did he know Eddie Vinson?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-11-17
items.q: Sometimes we used to get him to play... he'd be sick. But he didn't play with no regular band... I'd say that.

ctx.x: Tell him I heard he had a fight with Corny.

Say, he heard you had a fight with Corny. I think I heard about that. I think it was on my birthday that night, I got drunk, you know. And Tony told me to stop playing, you know. Stop drinking. I said, oh, you ain't got nothing to do with me. I said, the white people, they was giving it to me, helping me to celebrate. And Tony got mad. I said, you big son got busted. I said, go ahead, sit on, sit on, sit on. And then after he told me to come over, you know. Zip would play with his dad, you know. You know Zip,…
Tell him I heard that when Cornish swung at him, he'd run between his legs.
